title: How a Submarine Works in 60 Seconds 🌊⚓ #shorts
description:
A modern attack submarine can dive around 500 meters deep and still come back up. It floods ballast tanks with seawater to sink, uses trim tanks to hover at neutral buoyancy, and steers with hydroplanes. To surface, compressed air blows the water back out. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#submarine #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A modern attack submarine can dive around *500 meters* deep, and still come back up.

steps.label: Ballast
steps.text: The secret is *ballast tanks*. On the surface, they're full of air, so the sub floats.

steps.label: Dive
steps.text: To dive, *vents* open. Seawater floods in, and the sub gets heavier than the water around it.

steps.label: Trim
steps.text: Smaller *trim tanks* move water back and forth to hold it perfectly level, at *neutral buoyancy*.

steps.label: Planes
steps.text: Short wings called *hydroplanes* tilt the nose up or down to steer the dive.

steps.label: Surface
steps.text: To come up, *compressed air* blasts the water out of the tanks, and the sub rises.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Flood, balance, *blow*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
